title.en: Find the relative velocity of two bodies on a straight line

say.en: Sitting in a train, you see the train on the next track glide backwards, though both are leaving the station. Velocity always depends on who is watching. In this lesson: Define relative velocity.
Find the relative velocity of two bodies on a straight line.
Solve chase and meeting problems.

title.en: Velocity of B as seen from A

body.en: If A moves with *velocity* $v_A$ and B with $v_B$ along the same line, B seen from A moves with $v_{BA} = v_B - v_A$. Likewise A seen from B moves with $v_{AB} = v_A - v_B = -v_{BA}$. Signs give direction: choose one direction as positive and keep to it.

narration.en: If A moves with velocity $v_A$ and B with $v_B$ along the same line, B seen from A moves with $v_{BA} = v_B - v_A$. Likewise A seen from B moves with $v_{AB} = v_A - v_B = -v_{BA}$. Signs give direction: choose one direction as positive and keep to it.

say.en: If A moves with velocity v A and B with v B along the same line, B seen from A moves with v BA equals v B minus v A. Likewise A seen from B moves with v AB equals v A minus v B equals minus v BA. Signs give direction: choose one direction as positive and keep to it. Same direction: subtract the speeds.
Opposite directions: add the speeds.
v AB equals -v BA.

say.en: Relative velocity on a line.

problem.en: Car B is 60 m ahead of car A. A moves at 20 m/s and B at 10 m/s in the same direction. When does A catch B, and how far has A moved?

steps.en: Relative velocity of A with respect to B: 20 − 10 = 10 m/s.
The gap of 60 m closes at 10 m/s: t = 60/10 = 6 s.

answer.en: After 6 s, when A has moved 120 m

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Car B is 60 m ahead of car A. A moves at 20 m/s and B at 10 m/s in the same direction. When does A catch B, and how far has A moved?

say.en: Let us solve this together. Car B is 60 metres ahead of car A. A moves at 20 metres per second and B at 10 metres per second in the same direction. When does A catch B, and how far has A moved?
Relative velocity of A with respect to B: 20 minus 10 equals 10 metres per second.
The gap of 60 metres closes at 10 metres per second: t equals 60 over 10 equals 6 seconds.
Distance moved by A equals 20 times 6 equals 120 metres.
So the answer is After 6 seconds, when A has moved 120 metres.

problem.en: Two trains 200 m and 150 m long move towards each other on parallel tracks at 54 km/h and 72 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?

steps.en: To cross completely, the relative distance is the sum of the lengths: 350 m.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Two trains 200 m and 150 m long move towards each other on parallel tracks at 54 km/h and 72 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?

say.en: Let us solve this together. Two trains 200 metres and 150 metres long move towards each other on parallel tracks at 54 kilometres per hour and 72 kilometres per hour. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
Relative speed equals 54 plus 72 equals 126 kilometres per hour equals 35 metres per second.
To cross completely, the relative distance is the sum of the lengths: 350 metres.
t equals 350 over 35 equals 10 seconds.
So the answer is 10 seconds.

narration.en: Car B is sixty metres ahead and moves at ten metres per second. What speed must car A have to catch it in exactly six seconds?

prompt.en: Car B starts 60 m ahead and keeps 10 m/s. Choose the speed of car A so that it draws level with B exactly 6 s after the start. Lock in to run the race.

explanation.en: The gap of 60 m must close in 6 s, so v_A − 10 = 10 m/s and v_A = 20 m/s.

hint.en: The gap closes at the relative velocity v_A − v_B.

body.en: To find B as seen from A, imagine giving both bodies an extra velocity −v_A. A stops, and B is left with v_B − v_A. Chase problems then become: gap ÷ relative speed.

say.en: Stop the watcher. To find B as seen from A, imagine giving both bodies an extra velocity -v A. A stops, and B is left with v B - v A. Chase problems then become: gap divided by relative speed.
